solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Servant to work in Foreign Office with little Mary

indicators.note: the word for work is placed inside the abbreviation for Foreign Office

parts.note: to work is to act, as on stage
Little Mary is an old jocular name for the stomach, here the tummy shortened to tum

explanation.surface: A domestic helper taken on at the Foreign Office alongside a young girl called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is a dated British euphemism for the stomach (from a J.M. Barrie play), giving TUM rather than a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A general servant or employee who does all kinds of jobs is the Latin-derived term meaning 'do everything'.

clue.text: A free version of BBC

parts.note: to free something tied is to untie it

explanation.surface: A free-to-view take on the British Broadcasting Corporation.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately nicknamed after a fussy elderly relative, so this pet name is a version of its title.

clue.text: Work round wide cloth

indicators.note: the word for work goes round the letter for wide

parts.note: to till is to work the soil
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Someone works around a broad piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong woven fabric with diagonal ribs, used for jeans and trousers, is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Conductor takes opera to Northern Ireland twice

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: twice says the abbreviation for Northern Ireland appears two times in a row

explanation.surface: A conductor brings an opera production to Belfast for two runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral conductor, who indeed conducted Puccini's operas.

clue.text: Something splendid by Lake Poet

parts.note: a marvel is something wonderful
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A wonderful thing written by one of the Lake Poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Poet' suggests Wordsworth or Coleridge; the phrase must be split, Lake giving L.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Marvell was a seventeenth-century English metaphysical poet.

clue.text: In rough sea, fun is dangerous

indicators.note: rough sea suggests churning, so the letters of sea and fun are tossed about

explanation.surface: Swimming for fun in choppy seas is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns SEA and FUN into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not safe is risky or hazardous, a direct synonym of dangerous.

clue.text: Terrible clue right cause of suffering

indicators.note: a terrible clue is a mangled one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver complains that a dreadful clue is a real source of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like a verdict on the clue, but it is the anagram signal, and the scrambled letters come before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sore, such as one in the stomach lining, causes pain and so is a cause of suffering.

clue.text: A gherkin's pickled, getting smaller

indicators.note: a pickled vegetable is preserved and altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A gherkin shrivels as it sits in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduction in size, as of cloth in the wash, is the process of getting smaller.

clue.text: The ability to choose to skip the end of a film about a whale

indicators.note: skipping the end means the title's last letter is dropped

parts.note: Free Willy is a 1993 film about a killer whale

explanation.surface: Someone decides not to sit through the finale of a whale movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip the end of' drops the Y from FREE WILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophically, the power to act by one's own choice rather than by fate is the capacity to decide freely.

clue.text: Becomes a zombie apparently in clothing not normally seen

definitions.meaning: to come back from the dead is jokingly to reverse dying
underwear is clothing hidden beneath outer garments

explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is worn out of sight, and the word split as UN-DIES jokingly describes a corpse coming back as a zombie.

clue.text: Judge to change arrangement around front of court

indicators.note: the word for rearranging goes around the opening letter of court

parts.note: to reorder is to change the arrangement of something

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of court is taken

explanation.surface: A judge orders the courtroom to be rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a part-time judge in the English courts, so the title names a kind of judge.

clue.text: Vehicle left overturned gets royal distance without current providing power

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the distance word wraps the reversed vehicle and left

parts.note: Edinburgh's Royal Mile, so a distance of a mile

indicators.note: overturned means the word for vehicle with the letter for left is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car crashes and turns over beside Edinburgh's Royal Mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, so MILE goes round LRAC. 'current' seems to belong with 'without' as I (electrical current), but it opens the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The fast channel of water that drives a mill wheel is a current harnessed for power.

clue.text: Celebrity split almost immediately being covered up

indicators.note: the word for immediately is covered by the shortened word for split around it
almost means the last letter of the word for split is dropped

parts.note: to rend is to split or tear
now means immediately

explanation.surface: A famous person's split was hushed up almost at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims REND to REN, which covers NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame or widespread acclaim is what celebrity means in its abstract sense.

clue.text: Delay frivolous charge with impediment

indicators.note: a speech impediment, a lisp, makes each s sound come out as sh when the phrase is spoken

parts.note: silly means frivolous and a sally is a sudden charge out by troops

explanation.surface: Someone holds things up with a trivial accusation and a hindrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with impediment' lisps both S sounds in SILLY SALLY into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither and procrastinate is to put off a decision, an informal word for delay.

clue.text: Requested to leave first and go off — like this?

definitions.text: Requested to leave first and go off — like this?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for requested is told to leave

parts.note: asked means requested
to addle is to go off, as an egg goes rotten

explanation.surface: Someone asked to depart first wonders whether to rush away in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave first' drops the opening letter. The whole clue also describes the act: told to go first, you hurry off.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave in a hurry, scampering off, is the informal sense of this word.

clue.text: It may provide deal to get tax back

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
the spine is the back

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a deal to recover tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal here is softwood timber, not an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is fir or pine timber, and this conifer is one tree that supplies it.

clue.text: Rubber glove finally in widespread application

indicators.note: the closing letter of glove is placed inside the phrase for widespread application

parts.note: mass use is widespread application

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of glove

explanation.surface: Rubber gloves are in common use.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubber means one who rubs, not latex.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives massages rubs her clients, so she is literally a rubber.

clue.text: Where a lot will get squiffy with gin?

definitions.text: Where a lot will get squiffy with gin?

parts.words: Where a lot will get squiffy with gin?
parts.note: a pub where many people get tipsy on gin, also the pool where a herd (a lot) drinks

explanation.definitionFit: A pub or bar is jocularly named after the pool where wild animals gather to drink.

clue.text: See sign misspelt name of group

indicators.note: misspelt says the letters of see sign are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a sign with a band's name spelt wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A British rock band fronted by Peter Gabriel and later Phil Collins bore this name, also the Bible's first book.

clue.text: Coming out with pithy saying

indicators.note: out signals the letters of coming are set out of order

explanation.surface: Someone comes out with a terse remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech expressed in brief, cryptic maxims or aphorisms is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Like liberal TV presenter not on the level

parts.note: as means like
Ant McPartlin, of Ant and Dec, is a British TV presenter

explanation.surface: A left-leaning TV host seems dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' means sloping, not dishonest. Ant and Dec are a popular British presenting duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying at an angle or slope, rather than horizontal, means not being on the level.

clue.text: Request for another card from fool holding spades

indicators.note: the word for fool holds the letter for spades inside

parts.note: a twit is a fool
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player calls for another card from a foolish player holding spades.
explanation.walkthrough: In pontoon (a British card game like blackjack), saying 'twist' asks for another card.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game pontoon, this word is what a player says to be dealt a further card.

clue.text: Head of Enterprise perhaps nobody detains a short time

indicators.note: the phrase for nobody holds the short time inside it

parts.note: no one means nobody
sec, short for second, is a short time

explanation.surface: No one holds up the boss of a business for even a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Enterprise' looks like a company boss; Enterprise is a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed front end of a rocket or spacecraft such as the Enterprise is its head.

clue.text: Maybe Rhodes scholar's second with infestation turning up

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of scholar's
in a down clue turning up means the word for infestation is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lice are an infestation

explanation.surface: A Rhodes scholar finds a second outbreak of lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhodes scholar' reads as one phrase, but Rhodes alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Rhodes, the colonialist who founded the Rhodes scholarships, is an example of a man with this first name.

clue.text: For trattoria, say, prepares tomatoes and minor items

definitions.meaning: an Italian restaurant may get its tomatoes dried in the sun
miscellaneous small things of little importance

explanation.definitionFit: Assorted small things are odds and ends, and split as SUN-DRIES the word describes preparing tomatoes Italian-style.

clue.text: Money received in church securing honour

indicators.note: the church abbreviation secures the honour inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Cash comes in to the church to pay for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings or revenue are money that comes in, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Most recent bank getting electronic for a time

indicators.note: for says the letter for electronic stands in place of a and time

parts.note: NatWest is a British high-street bank
a gives A and time gives T
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A bank goes electronic for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: NatWest is a major British bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of new describes the latest, freshest thing.

clue.text: Detective Her Majesty left in surprise

indicators.note: the queen's initials and the letter for left go inside the word for surprise

parts.note: a shock is a surprise
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A detective leaves the Queen astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' tempts as part of the answer; Her Majesty as a whole gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Conan Doyle's Holmes is the archetypal fictional detective, known by this first name.
